title: Judge the experience, not the storage
statement: Judge only what changes the student's experience, and never fail an item for how its data is stored.
example: A judge flagged three equivalent answers to a single blank as if the item had several blanks.
detail: The judge misread a valid list of equivalent answers to one blank as several blanks and marked the item down, so a guard now restores those scores when the nested lists are the only issue cited (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/tests/test_issue_390_fillin_accepted_answers.py`). Version 2.6.6 added a base rule that the schema is irrelevant whenever a student would have the same experience however the data is structured (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/_base_evaluation.txt`), and turned a guard that failed answers for not matching a renderer's format into a no-op, since that is a platform concern rather than one of question quality (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/evaluators/guards.py`).
against: Version 2.6.3 still failed items for passage text placed in the question field (`icloud-work/inceptbench-latest/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/sat_rw_evaluation.txt`, line 27); answer options written into the stem as well as the options field are still penalised, which fits the rule because the student sees them twice (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/evaluators/question.py`, lines 700-701).

evidence.quote: If the same question, asked of a student, would have the same pedagogical experience regardless of how the JSON is structured, the schema is irrelevant.

The evaluator incorrectly flags FILL_IN questions where accepted_answers contains multiple single-element lists (e.g. [["3"], ["3/1"], ["6/2"]]) as having multiple blanks, when in fact this is the valid platform format for multiple equivalent answers to a single blank (list[answer_set][blank_index]).
Renderer / UI schema compliance is a platform concern, not a question-quality concern, so InceptBench no longer scores on it
However, the engine does NOT render `node.definition` as visible or spoken text to the child on this node.
they are inputs to the adapter, not what the student sees.
